issue_paraphrase: An HTTP response that comes back with an empty body but declares a zstd content encoding makes httpx raise an unexpected decoding error whenever the body is read: the library complains that the compressed data is incomplete even though the server deliberately sent no bytes at all. Clients that talk to endpoints which return zero-length responses carrying that header crash on reading the body instead of getting an empty result. The failure shows up the moment the empty body is materialized, whether through response.content, iter_bytes, or a plain read.
fix_summary: Added a `seen_data` flag to ZStandardDecoder: when no data has ever been fed (empty body) its flush() returns b'' immediately instead of consulting decompressor.eof and raising DecodingError. Added regression tests cover both the empty-body and the truncated-stream cases.
notes: Fast and fully offline (<1s). CRITICAL environment trap: if the zstandard package is not installed, httpx silently falls back to an identity decoder for Content-Encoding: zstd, and the bug does NOT reproduce (the repro would pass even at the parent). The task image must install zstandard. Verified with zstandard 0.23.x on Python 3.12. test_zstd_truncated is a pre-existing passing test; test_zstd_empty is the regression signal.

issue_paraphrase: Streaming the decoded text of an HTTP response in chunks produces a spurious empty piece at the end: iterating over the text of a response whose body arrives as multiple chunks yields an extra empty string after the actual content. Code that joins the yielded chunks to rebuild a document ends up with a trailing empty element that is not part of the response, and assertions over the exact chunk sequence fail. The extra piece appears only when the body is split across more than one chunk; single-piece bodies are unaffected.
fix_summary: TextChunker.decode() now returns an empty list instead of a list containing one empty string when the input text is empty, so Response.iter_text()/iter_lines() no longer emit a spurious '' chunk after the final flush. The now-unreachable yield paths in Response.iter_text and iter_lines were marked pragma: no cover, and a streaming regression test was added.

issue_paraphrase: The per-client timeout is silently ignored when a request is created directly as an httpx.Request instance instead of through the client's own request builder: sending a manually constructed request via client.send(...) runs with the default timeout even though the client was configured with a much smaller one, so operations that should be aborted almost immediately instead hang for the full default period and eventually succeed anyway. The same gap affects both the synchronous and the asynchronous client APIs. Programs that rely on a strict timeout to fail fast are left waiting regardless of their configured value.
fix_summary: Added BaseClient._set_timeout(request), which copies the client's configured timeout into request.extensions when the request does not already carry a timeout, and called it from both Client.send and AsyncClient.send before authentication handling. Manually built Request instances passed to send() now honor the client-level timeout instead of falling back to the default.
notes: Repro needs only loopback networking (localhost socket server), no external network; golden test spins an in-process uvicorn ASGI server (conftest fixture), also loopback-only. Test run takes ~2.2s at parent (server slow path sleeps 1.0s) and ~0.2s at fix. The golden test is @pytest.mark.anyio and runs once per backend (asyncio + trio) when both are installed, hence 2 failed/2 passed lines. Not flaky in local runs. The sync Client.send is fixed by the same commit, so a sync direct repro is the simplest oracle.
